name: Complex dynamics: iteration of rational functions (Julia and Fatou)
from: iteration theory of functional equations (Schroeder, Koenigs)
summary: Julia and Fatou independently studied iterated rational maps of the plane, introducing attractors, repellers and the sets now named after them.

name: Unipotent flows and the Oppenheim conjecture
summary: Values of indefinite quadratic forms at integer points are controlled by showing orbits of unipotent subgroups on homogeneous spaces are well-behaved.

name: Biometric mathematical statistics
summary: Pearson developed correlation and chi-square for biological data and founded Biometrika.

name: Analytic geometry (Descartes, Fermat)
summary: Geometric problems were translated into algebraic equations, solved and classified by degree.

name: Euler's Introductio
summary: Functions replaced curves as the object of calculus, with e^{ix} relation, exponentials and logs.

name: Transmission of Hindu-Arabic numerals to the Islamic world
summary: A treatise on Indian decimal calculation, later translated into Latin, spread the positional system and gave 'algorithm' its name.

name: Lorentz group and Minkowski spacetime: group theory enters physics
summary: Poincare showed Lorentz transformations form a group, Einstein derived them from two postulates, and Minkowski gave a tensor form of electrodynamics and showed Newtonian gravity incompatible.

name: Burnside's use of character theory for finite group theory
summary: Burnside applied Frobenius characters to prove the p^a q^b solvability theorem.

name: Noncommutative geometry
summary: Geometric invariants (cohomology, index theory) are extended to operator algebras viewed as spaces of noncommutative functions.

name: Computational complexity
summary: Resource-bounded computation was classified into hierarchies.
